newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says no EMU decision before debate.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says no EMU decision before debate.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said no binding decisions on European monetary union would be made before a full debate in the UK parliament ahead of the Dublin summit.

Dismissing what he called "inaccuracies and innuendos" in weekend press reports, he told parliament that a debate would take place before the summit, on a date to be announced by the Leader of the House.
"I repeat that no binding decisions will be taken in any forum, or were ever likely to be, until that debate has taken place," he told parliament.
The Dublin summit takes place on December 13 and 14.

Clarke said that throughout the EMU negotiations, he had shown proper regard for the interests and procedures of parliament and "a desire to achieve a sensible and acceptable outcome on the stability pact."
